title: Add TypeScript template scaffold (RAG + agent) with minimal server + streaming handling
author: Dana Lo
release_notes: New: TypeScript quickstart template scaffold (server + streaming response handling) to mirror the Python RAG/agent layout. Adds minimal dev/prod scripts, env config, and README skeleton.
description:
Context: We have a Python RAG+agent quickstart scaffold landing first; this PR creates the matching TypeScript/Node scaffold so we can iterate on streaming stability, tool calling, retriever adapters, and OTel instrumentation in follow-on PRs.

What’s included (TS scaffold):
- New template directory: templates/rag-agent-ts/ mirroring the Python project structure (config, server entrypoint, agent loop placeholder, retrieval placeholder).
- Minimal HTTP server with a single chat endpoint and streaming support.
- Streaming robustness basics: abort handling + best-effort cleanup when the client disconnects.
- Environment/config parsing with explicit schema + .env.example.
- Repo-standard scripts and tooling: TypeScript build, lint/format, and a minimal “smoke” script that exercises streaming locally.

Design notes:
- This scaffold intentionally stays provider-light: it uses the Redwood TS SDK directly today (no extra abstraction layer yet). We’ll align provider abstraction/model pinning after the Python/TS templates converge on the same config surface.
- Observability is intentionally minimal here (log structure only). Full OTel spans/metrics will be added in the dedicated instrumentation PR to avoid mixing concerns.

Local run:
1) cd templates/rag-agent-ts
2) cp .env.example .env  (set REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, REDWOOD_MODEL)
3) pnpm install
4) pnpm dev
5) curl -N http://localhost:3000/chat -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"message":"Explain continuous batching."}'

Illustrative snippet (streaming + abort):
- src/server.ts
  - Creates an AbortController per request
  - Hooks res.on('close') to abort upstream streaming
  - Streams tokens to the client as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for now; we can swap to SSE once docs settle on a single format.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-4183):
- Tool calling + structured output parsing (PR-109)
- OTel tracing/metrics + Redwood-specific conventions (ENG-4184)
- Retry/timeout defaults aligned with safe-defaults policy (ENG-4184/ENG-4186)

Checklist:
- [x] Template boots locally on Node 18/20
- [x] Streaming endpoint supports incremental output and handles client disconnect
- [x] .env.example included; no secrets committed
- [x] README skeleton + troubleshooting placeholders
- [ ] OTel instrumentation (separate PR)
- [ ] Retriever adapters + indexing flow (separate PR)

Notes for reviewers:
- Naming: I matched env var names with the Python scaffold where possible (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, REDWOOD_MODEL). If we want a different config surface for TS, I’d prefer we decide once and apply to both.

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-4183 (Ship RAG+agent quickstart - TypeScript)
- Related PRs: pr-101 (Python scaffold), pr-102 (OTel + log redaction), pr-103 (timeouts/retries defaults)
